Used to play quite frequently months ago but sometime around June/July, it started crashing every time I got past "Logging in to User Center" or whatever it says. I have an IT background so I've been on and off trying whatever I can think of to fix this problem and play the game <a:manscrying:796293907788988446> Here's a link to the log (essentially identical every time it crashes): https://pastebin.com/VmpqqMJ5

What I've tried so far:
Steam file integrity verification and full clean reinstall
All overlays disabled (Steam, Discord, NVIDIA, Windows Game Bar)
Unity Graphics Jobs disabled via boot.config (gfx-enable-gfx-jobs=0)
NVIDIA power management set to "Prefer maximum performance"
DLDSR fully disabled
Forced dGPU via Windows Graphics settings (system has a secondary AMD iGPU)
Two different NVIDIA driver versions
GPU/driver stability confirmed clean via FurMark stress test (10+ min, stable clocks/temps, zero errors)
No corresponding TDR/driver-reset event in Windows Event Viewer System log at time of crash — the device removal appears client-side, not an actual driver crash
Deleted all local PlayerPrefs/cache data (AppData/LocalLow/Morimens, com.Morimens.pc, com_Morimens_pc)

content:
There are quite a few people who enjoy the game and want to play it but lack the skill, so they spend money to boost their characters' power; however, they are now quitting because inflation has made even that approach too difficult to sustain.

Doesn't that make sense? They find the game fun but challenging, so they spend money to strengthen their characters. After all, if they had wanted a difficult gameplay experience, they wouldn't have needed to make their characters powerful in the first place.

It is truly disheartening to watch them leave. A player base that spends money is essential for the game to keep running, so their departure makes it difficult to sustain the game. It breaks my heart to see players—whom I personally recruited to the game—posting in the community about quitting for this very reason.
